items.summary: A fix let Alertmanager reload its own redacted config when a Slack receiver posts updates. We reproduced the bug on main, then found the same break in the global Slack settings, which the fix didn't cover yet.

Cockpit's bridge was running out of file descriptors because it never closed its pipes to finished processes. We traced every path that closes a process to show the fix can't close a pipe the event loop is still reading, or close the same one twice.
Checked a sitemap fix against the whole site and found no page it would drop yet, so we asked which page prompted it.

A fix lifting the WebSocket message limit for browser DERP clients said every peer was an authenticated server, which isn't true on the relay side. We traced the reads end to end and showed it's still safe there, because the DERP and Noise frame limits do the bounding.
Checked a fix for dead Marathon links in the config docs, and found two more links to the same retired site in the Marathon discovery code, with archived copies to point them at.
Confirmed against the live docs site that a fix for broken query-docs anchors points at headings that really exist.

Fiber's HSTS advisory named a Go module path that doesn't exist at v3, so scanners checking fiber/v3 missed it. We proved the right path from the module proxy, showed v2 isn't affected, and proposed the fix.
Caddy's advisory for the CVE-2026-30852 fix bypass listed no patched version. We traced the fix to 2.11.3 and sent a correction with the fix PR, so scanners can stop flagging upgraded servers.
Vitess's advisory marked the already-patched 0.23.6 as vulnerable. We checked each fix commit against its release tag and proposed both ranges to match Vitess's own advisory.
Timed the HTTP Request node's batching against a test server and found a docs example promising one request per second actually sends 50 at once unless you change one more setting.
Showed the email notifier can still hang on a mail server that accepts the connection but never replies, and tested a two-line fix that stops it on time.
Started Jenkins with JKS, PKCS12 and JCEKS keystores to confirm the new HTTPS docs say which formats work and from which version.
Built the Linux packages before and after a fix under two build setups and confirmed every file now installs with the same permissions wherever it was built.
Found a reliable way to trigger a race the maintainers couldn't pin down, where pausing the logs page left a journalctl running, and sent a fix.
Reworked the Ubuntu logo fix after review so Ubuntu 22.04 keeps its logo, and tested it on 22.04 and 24.04.
Checked that every other DNS manager call is safe in builds without DNS, after a fix for a crash on queries to 100.100.100.100.
Confirmed from Go's source why the API left multipart temp files on disk, and showed the test checks the helper but not the fix.
Checked all five replaced docs links: every old one is a 404 and every new one loads.
Checked the TLS chain of every host the site build downloads from, so turning certificate checks back on won't break it.
Found that a fix for serve redirects would let a request starting with two slashes redirect to another host, and suggested a one-line guard.
Traced why the new journal test fails on every CentOS Stream run but passes on Fedora, and suggested a way that doesn't depend on PATH.
Showed a second pass of the serve hostname fix still failed for mixed-case SNI at the certificate lookup, then approved the third.
Tested the plain-HTTP serve Host fix against odd Host headers, and found its comment's claim about Go's TLS doesn't hold.
Checked the new storage lifecycle advice against n8n's code, and found a rule that would expire chat attachments still in use.
Checked every meta label in the service discovery docs fix against the labels the code actually sets.
Traced why TS_EXTRA_ARGS stops applying after the first boot with TS_AUTH_ONCE, and gave three workarounds.
Sent the fix for the broken Ubuntu logos in the ws container, after the reporter confirmed it on Ubuntu 26.04.
Built the CORS default-origin fix and its base, and checked every origin setting against the API with curl.
Tested the new deb822 apt setup on four distros, and found the page's indent breaks it when copied.
Checked what's left of a security-group docs issue after an earlier fix, and asked the claimant if they're still on it.
Checked the queue-mode upgrade steps against the source, and found db:revert exits 0 even when it refuses.
Confirmed an old fork issue is already resolved upstream, and suggested closing it.
Checked a DNS name fix against every short string, with no mismatches where the base had 100.
Showed the planned fix for an npm install error would drop bindings from the Docker image again.
Found a journal query leaves its pipeline running after close, and tested a fix.
Checked the EPEL package rename in Rocky 8, 9 and 10, and found EPEL 8 has no package at all.
Reproduced broken Ubuntu logos in the ws container, and tested a fix for both themes.
Retested the checksum work at the author's request, and confirmed the dropped pin now shows in the log.
Reproduced an allow list bug through analyze(), and found terms the planned fix can't compile, before it was sent.
Tested a new install checksum against a real release, and found the pin silently drops when set before sudo.
Confirmed a spilled query's len() is fixed on master, by building before and after, so a maintainer can close the issue.
Reproduced a false "does not exist" on hosts without /etc/mtab through a real OVAL scan, and confirmed the fix.
Ran a real scan to show invalid results on main and valid ones with the fix, for addresses ending in ::.
Two small things found by re-running the install script on a fapolicyd host.
Why a kernel config check didn't fire on Linux 6.18, and the symbol that makes it work.
A review confirming the fix for an allow list that dropped real findings, email addresses included.
The reproduction a maintainer asked for: a denial that aureport silently left out.
Tracing a reported Langfuse 404 back through the code to a likely cause.
